summary: Monkey's rebellion and cultivation, then a comic pilgrimage with Tripitaka, Pigsy, and Sandy through demon-infested lands to win the scriptures and Buddhahood.

hunger.why: Pigsy's gluttony, begging for alms that triggers episode after episode, stolen immortal peaches and ginseng fruit, and demons craving Tripitaka's flesh run throughout.

thirst.why: Pilgrims search for water on the road, and drinking from the Child-and-Mother River leaves Tripitaka and Pigsy pregnant.

feeling-cold-hot.why: Monkey survives Laozi's furnace, and the Flaming Mountain episode blocks the road with unbearable heat for several chapters.

sleepiness.why: The pilgrims lodge at inns and temples, but fatigue is rarely a theme.

curiosity.why: Monkey leaps into the Water Curtain Cave, sails off to seek immortality, and the pilgrimage crosses unknown kingdoms and mountains to India.

explanation-seeking.why: Monkey repeatedly works out which demon they face and consults Heaven about its origin, and exposes the usurper of Wuji kingdom.

skill-acquisition.why: Monkey learns the seventy-two transformations and cloud somersault from Subodhi, and the whole journey is cultivation toward Buddhahood.

play.why: Monkey's mischief, playful transformations, and pranks on Pigsy keep the tone of a game.

resource-accumulation.why: Monkey extracts the golden staff and armor from the dragon kings, and the scriptures are the prize that ends the quest.

resource-foraging.why: Begging for food, finding water, gathering fruit, and the scriptures themselves make searching for resources a constant.

mental-time-travel.why: Guanyin plans the pilgrimage and its eighty-one ordeals, and Monkey schemes before each fight.

fear-of-predators.why: Tiger, spider, scorpion, and monster demons hunt the pilgrims to eat Tripitaka's flesh in nearly every episode.

fear-of-aggressors.why: Monkey battles the heavenly host, and demon kings and their armies attack the pilgrims chapter after chapter.

fear-of-heights.why: Cloud flights, mountain crags, and Monkey's imprisonment under Five Phases Mountain involve heights but little vertigo.

disgust.why: Spider demons, filthy caves, Monkey urinating on Buddha's palm, and the male pregnancy river evoke contamination.

pain-aversion.why: The golden headband torments Monkey, Pigsy is beaten, demons boil and torture captives, and Monkey burns in the furnace.

pride.why: Monkey names himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven, boasts of every feat, and all four pilgrims win titles as Buddhas and arhats.

shame.why: Pigsy is shamed when his lust is exposed, and Monkey is disgraced when banished by Tripitaka.

moral-pride.why: Tripitaka clings to vows of chastity and non-violence even when they endanger him, and refuses the queen of the Women's Kingdom.

guilt.why: Tripitaka regrets expelling Monkey unjustly, and Pigsy repents his lapses before Guanyin.

warmth.why: Guanyin's kindness rescues the pilgrims, and Monkey's loyalty to Tripitaka survives every banishment.

moral-blame.why: Tripitaka condemns Monkey's killings, Monkey exposes false monks and tyrannical kings, and Heaven judges Monkey's rebellion.

moral-praise.why: Rescued kingdoms honor the pilgrims, and Buddha rewards their merit with holy titles.

revenge.why: Monkey assails Heaven for insulting him, and the Bull Demon King seeks vengeance for his son Red Boy.

forgiveness.why: Tripitaka takes Monkey back after each banishment, Guanyin converts demons rather than destroying them, and Buddha pardons the pilgrims' past sins.

compassion.why: Guanyin, bodhisattva of compassion, guides the quest, and Tripitaka pities every sufferer, including demons in disguise.

affiliation.why: Monkey gathers monkey subjects, swears brotherhood with demon kings, and the four pilgrims and the dragon horse join one by one.

friendship.why: The bond among Monkey, Pigsy, Sandy, and Tripitaka, with its quarrels and rescues, carries the whole journey.

sadness.why: Monkey weeps when banished and when Tripitaka seems dead, and mourns his slaughtered monkeys.

humor.why: Pigsy's greed and lust, Monkey's tricks, bickering disciples, and absurd transformations make the novel comic throughout.

embarrassment.why: Pigsy is caught courting spider women, Monkey is humiliated under Buddha's hand, and Tripitaka blushes before seductresses.

reasoning.why: Monkey argues with Tripitaka about killing demons and spars verbally with heavenly officials and Buddhist patriarchs.

coalitional-affiliation.why: The pilgrim band, Monkey's monkey kingdom, the heavenly bureaucracy, and demon alliances define every side.

status-seeking.why: Monkey revolts over his lowly stable post, demands the title Great Sage, and the ending ranks the pilgrims by merit.

envy.why: Monkey covets the immortals' peaches and elixir, and Pigsy resents Monkey's favor with Tripitaka.

anger.why: Monkey's fury at Heaven's slights, Tripitaka's anger at his killings, and the Bull Demon King's rage drive many conflicts.

hatred.why: Demons loathe Monkey, and Monkey gloats over defeated foes, but hatred is secondary to comedy.

romantic-affiliation.why: The queen of the Women's Kingdom courts Tripitaka, and Pigsy takes a wife at Gao village.

sexual-attraction.why: Pigsy lusts after every woman, female demons seduce Tripitaka, and the bodhisattvas test the pilgrims with beautiful daughters.

long-term-love.why: Pigsy's marriage at Gao village is brief; lasting romantic commitment is nearly absent.

desire.why: Pigsy's unceasing lust and the demons' pursuit of Tripitaka's yang energy are recurring motifs.

romantic-jealousy.why: Princess Iron Fan resents the Bull Demon King's concubine, the Jade-Faced Fox.

sexual-jealousy.why: Iron Fan's rivalry with the fox concubine is the only instance.

sexual-disgust.why: Female demons try to force Tripitaka into marriage to steal his essence, and Pigsy's harassment of Chang'e earned his exile.

parental-care.why: Monkey protects his monkey subjects as children, and the pilgrims rescue the children of the Bhiksu kingdom.

parental-investment.why: Subodhi trains Monkey, and Tripitaka instructs his disciples as master and father figure.

familial-love.why: Tripitaka's reunion with his mother and vengeance for his father, and the Bull Demon King's family ties, appear in episodes.
